title: E-2 Investor Visa
tagline: Start or Invest in a U.S. Business and Live in the United States Legally
overview: The E-2 Treaty Investor Visa allows eligible foreign nationals from treaty countries to live and work in the United States by investing in a qualifying U.S. business — ideal for entrepreneurs, investors, and business owners who want to establish or purchase a business in the United States.

benefits.title: Live & Work Legally
benefits.description: Legally live and work in the United States while actively directing your business operations.

benefits.title: Start or Buy a Business
benefits.description: Start a new company, purchase an existing U.S. business, or invest in one where you hold operational control.

benefits.title: Spouse Work Authorization
benefits.description: Your spouse may receive E-2 dependent status and may be eligible to work in the United States.

benefits.title: Children's Education
benefits.description: Unmarried children under 21 may attend U.S. schools, colleges, and universities on dependent status.

benefits.title: Renewable Status
benefits.description: Renewable as long as the business remains active and compliant — no fixed maximum stay period.

benefits.title: Faster Processing
benefits.description: Faster processing compared to many other business immigration options, with both consular and USCIS pathways.

eligibility.title: Treaty Country Citizenship
eligibility.description: You must be a citizen of a country that has an E-2 treaty with the United States, holding a valid passport from an eligible treaty country.

eligibility.title: Substantial Investment
eligibility.description: You must invest a substantial amount into a real and active U.S. business. Many successful E-2 cases involve approximately $100,000 or more depending on the business type.

eligibility.title: Investment Must Be At Risk
eligibility.description: The E-2 investment must be committed and at risk for the purpose of generating profit — funds must be spent or legally committed before the visa decision.

eligibility.title: Ownership or Operational Control
eligibility.description: You must generally own at least 50% of the business or have sufficient operational control to direct and manage the enterprise.

eligibility.title: Active and Legitimate Business
eligibility.description: The business must be a real, active, and operating commercial enterprise. Passive investments like property holdings or stocks typically do not qualify.

eligibility.title: Non-Marginal Enterprise
eligibility.description: The business should generate more than minimal income and ideally support job creation and economic activity in the United States.

eligibility.title: Intent to Depart
eligibility.description: The applicant must show an intention to depart the United States when E-2 status ends, though the visa may be renewed if the business continues to qualify.

process.title: Business Selection & Investment Planning
process.description: We help you evaluate business options, investment structure, ownership model, and visa suitability. You may choose to start a new company, purchase an existing business, or invest in a qualifying U.S. enterprise.

process.title: Business Setup & Strategy
process.description: Our team assists with business planning, company formation guidance, investment documentation, operational structure, and preparation of a strong E-2 business strategy.

process.title: Document Preparation
process.description: A successful E-2 application requires detailed documentation — including proof of funds, source of investment, business plan, ownership documents, lease agreements, invoices, contracts, and licenses.

process.title: E-2 Application Filing
process.description: Depending on your situation, the E-2 application may be filed through a U.S. consulate abroad or, in certain cases, through USCIS for a change of status inside the United States.

process.title: Embassy Interview Preparation
process.description: For consular cases, the applicant must attend an interview at the U.S. Embassy or Consulate. We provide structured interview preparation to help you explain your business and investment plans confidently.

process.title: Visa Approval & U.S. Entry
process.description: Once approved, you may enter the United States to direct, operate, and grow your E-2 business. Your spouse and children may also enter as E-2 dependents.

title: EB-1A Extraordinary Ability
tagline: Achieve Your U.S. Green Card Through Extraordinary Ability (EB-1A)
overview: If you’ve reached the top of your field in science, business, arts, education, or athletics — the EB-1A visa could be your path to a U.S. Green Card. The EB-1A visa is designed for individuals with extraordinary achievements recognized at a national or international level. This category allows you to self-petition without needing a U.S. job offer or employer sponsorship.

benefits.title: No Job Offer Required
benefits.description: You can self-petition. No U.S. employer sponsorship needed.

benefits.title: Fastest Green Card Route
benefits.description: Priority category with faster processing compared to other Green Card paths.

benefits.title: Freedom & Flexibility
benefits.description: Work or live anywhere in the U.S. without restrictions.

benefits.title: Permanent Residency for Family
benefits.description: Spouse and children under 21 are also eligible for permanent residency.

eligibility.title: Major Awards or Recognition
eligibility.description: Major awards or recognition in your field at a national or international level.

eligibility.title: Published Work in Top Media or Journals
eligibility.description: Published work in top media outlets or peer-reviewed journals in your field.

eligibility.title: Membership in Associations
eligibility.description: Membership in associations requiring outstanding achievement as a condition of entry.

eligibility.title: Original Contributions of Major Significance
eligibility.description: Original contributions of major significance in your field recognized by peers and experts.

eligibility.title: High Salary or Remuneration
eligibility.description: High salary or remuneration for your expertise relative to others in the same field.

eligibility.title: Leading or Judging Work of Others
eligibility.description: Leading or judging the work of others in your area of expertise at a recognized level.

process.title: Profile Evaluation
process.description: We assess your achievements and eligibility against USCIS EB-1A criteria. Our team reviews your awards, publications, contributions, salary history, memberships, and other evidence to determine whether your profile meets the extraordinary ability standard.

process.title: Document Preparation
process.description: We prepare strong evidence to support your petition. This includes organizing proof of awards, media coverage, citations, contracts, and any other documentation that demonstrates your extraordinary ability and sustained national or international acclaim.

process.title: Recommendation Letters
process.description: Drafting powerful support letters from experts in your field. Well-crafted recommendation letters from credible, independent voices are one of the most important elements of a strong EB-1A petition, and we guide this process carefully.

process.title: Petition Filing
process.description: Managing the entire USCIS submission process. We handle Form I-140 preparation, organize the petition package, review all exhibits, and submit the complete filing on your behalf — ensuring accuracy and completeness at every step.

process.title: Follow-up Support
process.description: Guidance until your Green Card is approved. We monitor your case status, respond to any USCIS requests for evidence (RFE), and keep you informed at every stage — from petition receipt through final Green Card approval.

title: EB-2 (NIW – National Interest Waiver)
tagline: Get a US Green Card without employer sponsorship through EB-2 NIW
overview: The EB-2 National Interest Waiver (NIW) allows professionals with advanced degrees or exceptional ability to bypass the traditional employer sponsorship and labor certification process, provided their work is in the national interest of the United States.

benefits.title: Work Without Sponsorship
benefits.description: Self-petition your Green Card without needing a specific job offer or U.S. employer.

benefits.title: Based on National Benefit
benefits.description: Your expertise and proposed endeavor will broadly benefit the United States economy, education, or society.

benefits.title: Advanced Degree Advantage
benefits.description: Ideal for professionals holding Master's, PhDs, or Bachelor's with 5+ years of progressive experience.

benefits.title: PERM Labor Certification Waived
benefits.description: Avoid the lengthy and restrictive PERM labor certification process.

eligibility.title: Advanced Degree or Exceptional Ability
eligibility.description: Must hold an advanced degree (or equivalent) OR demonstrate exceptional ability in sciences, arts, or business.

eligibility.title: Substantial Merit and National Importance
eligibility.description: Your proposed work must have substantial merit and be of national importance to the U.S.

eligibility.title: Well-Positioned to Advance the Endeavor
eligibility.description: You must have the education, skills, and record of success to advance your proposed endeavor.

eligibility.title: Beneficial to Waive Job Offer
eligibility.description: It must be beneficial to the U.S. to waive the standard job offer and labor certification requirements.

process.title: Initial Assessment
process.description: Evaluating your academic credentials, professional experience, and proposed endeavor.

process.title: Strategy & Document Gathering
process.description: Building a comprehensive case proving national importance through citations, awards, and expert letters.

process.title: Petition Preparation
process.description: Drafting the legal arguments and organizing the I-140 petition for USCIS submission.

process.title: Filing & Follow-up
process.description: Submitting the application and handling any Requests for Evidence (RFE) until approval.

title: EB-3 (Skilled, Professional, and Unskilled Workers)
tagline: Secure Your U.S. Green Card through the EB-3 Program
overview: The EB-3 visa offers a direct path to permanent residency for skilled, professional, and unskilled workers seeking stable employment in the United States. It requires a permanent, full-time job offer and labor certification.

benefits.title: Permanent U.S. Employment
benefits.description: Secure a permanent job offer from a U.S. employer willing to sponsor your residency.

benefits.title: Skilled or Entry-Level Jobs
benefits.description: Pathways available for professionals with degrees, skilled workers with 2+ years of experience, and unskilled laborers.

benefits.title: Green Card Opportunity
benefits.description: Provides permanent residency status upon approval and entry/adjustment of status.

benefits.title: Family Dependent Benefits
benefits.description: Your spouse and unmarried children under 21 can join you in the United States.

eligibility.title: Valid U.S. Job Offer
eligibility.description: Must have a permanent, full-time job offer from a U.S. employer.

eligibility.title: Labor Certification (PERM)
eligibility.description: The employer must obtain an approved labor certification demonstrating a shortage of willing and qualified U.S. workers.

eligibility.title: Professionals
eligibility.description: Must possess a U.S. baccalaureate degree or foreign equivalent, and a job requiring that degree.

eligibility.title: Skilled Workers
eligibility.description: Must be able to perform work requiring a minimum of 2 years training or experience.

eligibility.title: Unskilled Workers (Other Workers)
eligibility.description: Must be capable of performing unskilled labor requiring less than 2 years training or experience.

process.title: Employer Sponsorship & Job Offer
process.description: Securing a qualifying job offer from a U.S. employer willing to act as your sponsor.

process.title: PERM Labor Certification
process.description: The employer completes the recruitment process and files the PERM application with the Department of Labor.

process.title: Form I-140 Petition
process.description: Once PERM is approved, the employer files the I-140 Immigrant Petition for Alien Worker with USCIS.

process.title: Adjustment of Status or Consular Processing
process.description: After I-140 approval and when a visa number is available, file for adjustment of status in the U.S. or undergo consular processing abroad.

title: EB-4 (Special Immigrants)
tagline: Special Immigrant Visas Including Religious Workers
overview: The EB-4 preference category is designed for 'Special Immigrants', which includes a wide variety of specific applicants such as religious workers, broadcasters, and certain government employees, offering them a pathway to U.S. permanent residency.

benefits.title: Religious Worker Visa
benefits.description: A dedicated pathway for ministers and non-minister religious workers to immigrate permanently.

benefits.title: Broad Eligibility Options
benefits.description: Covers a diverse range of special groups identified by U.S. immigration law.

benefits.title: Path to U.S. Residency
benefits.description: Results in a U.S. Green Card for the applicant and their eligible dependents.

eligibility.title: Qualifying Special Immigrant Category
eligibility.description: Must fall into one of the designated categories, such as Religious Worker, Special Immigrant Juvenile, or Broadcaster.

eligibility.title: Two-Year Membership (Religious Workers)
eligibility.description: For religious workers, you must have been a member of a religious denomination having a bona fide non-profit religious organization in the U.S. for at least two years immediately before filing.

eligibility.title: Employer Petition
eligibility.description: Most EB-4 categories require a U.S. employer to file Form I-360 on your behalf.

process.title: Determine Category Eligibility
process.description: Identify which specific EB-4 special immigrant category applies to your situation.

process.title: Form I-360 Petition
process.description: The employer or applicant (depending on category) files Form I-360 with supporting documentation.

process.title: Green Card Application
process.description: Upon I-360 approval, file for an adjustment of status if in the U.S. or apply for an immigrant visa through consular processing.

title: EB-5 (Investor Visa Program)
tagline: Invest and Secure U.S. Residency for Your Family
overview: The EB-5 Immigrant Investor Program allows foreign investors to obtain a U.S. Green Card by making a substantial capital investment in a U.S. commercial enterprise that creates jobs for American workers.

benefits.title: Invest and Get Residency
benefits.description: A direct path to a Green Card for those willing to make a qualifying investment.

benefits.title: No Sponsorship Needed
benefits.description: No need for employer sponsorship, family sponsorship, or extraordinary abilities.

benefits.title: Family Green Card Benefit
benefits.description: One investment qualifies the investor, spouse, and unmarried children under 21 for Green Cards.

benefits.title: Flexibility to Live Anywhere
benefits.description: EB-5 investors can live, work, and retire anywhere in the United States.

eligibility.title: Qualifying Capital Investment
eligibility.description: Must invest the required minimum amount ($800,000 in a Targeted Employment Area, or $1,050,000 elsewhere).

eligibility.title: Job Creation Requirement
eligibility.description: The investment must create or preserve at least 10 full-time jobs for qualifying U.S. workers within two years.

eligibility.title: Lawful Source of Funds
eligibility.description: Investors must thoroughly document that the capital invested was obtained through lawful means.

eligibility.title: At-Risk Investment
eligibility.description: The capital must be placed at risk in a new commercial enterprise or an approved Regional Center.

process.title: Select Investment Project
process.description: Choose between a direct investment or investing through a USCIS-approved Regional Center.

process.title: File Form I-526E / I-526
process.description: Submit the immigrant petition demonstrating the investment and lawful source of funds.

process.title: Conditional Green Card
process.description: Upon approval, undergo consular processing or adjustment of status to receive a 2-year conditional Green Card.

process.title: File Form I-829
process.description: At the end of the 2-year period, file to remove conditions by proving the investment was sustained and jobs were created, resulting in a permanent Green Card.

title: L1A (Executive & Manager Transfer Visa)
tagline: Transfer Key Executives and Managers to the U.S.
overview: The L-1A nonimmigrant visa enables a U.S. employer to transfer an executive or manager from one of its affiliated foreign offices to one of its offices in the United States, or to send an executive to establish a new affiliated office.

quick_facts.Spouse Benefits: L-2 Spouse may work in the U.S.

benefits.title: Transfer to U.S. Company Branch
benefits.description: Seamlessly move critical leadership from a foreign branch to the U.S. headquarters or affiliate.

benefits.title: Live & Work as Executive/Manager
benefits.description: Work legally in the U.S. while managing essential business operations.

benefits.title: Direct Pathway to Green Card (EB-1C)
benefits.description: L-1A holders often qualify for the EB-1C Green Card category, offering a streamlined path to permanent residency.

benefits.title: New Office Setup
benefits.description: Allows foreign companies to send a manager to the U.S. specifically to establish a new office.

eligibility.title: Qualifying Relationship
eligibility.description: There must be a qualifying relationship between the U.S. company and the foreign entity (parent, branch, subsidiary, or affiliate).

eligibility.title: One Year Continuous Employment
eligibility.description: The employee must have worked for the foreign company continuously for at least one year within the three years preceding admission.

eligibility.title: Executive or Managerial Capacity
eligibility.description: The employee must be entering the U.S. to provide services in an executive or managerial capacity.

process.title: Establish Qualifying Relationship
process.description: Document the corporate relationship between the foreign entity and the U.S. office.

process.title: File Form I-129
process.description: The U.S. employer files the L-1A petition with USCIS on behalf of the employee.

process.title: Visa Application
process.description: Once the petition is approved, the employee applies for the L-1A visa at a U.S. Embassy or Consulate.

title: All Immigration Services & Paperwork
tagline: Comprehensive Legal Form Assistance & End-to-End Support
overview: Beyond specific visa pathways, we offer comprehensive immigration services and paperwork assistance to ensure your applications, petitions, and responses to USCIS are handled with expert care and precision.

benefits.title: Complete File Preparation
benefits.description: We ensure your immigration file is organized, thorough, and accurately prepared.

benefits.title: Legal Form Assistance
benefits.description: Guidance on correctly filling out complex USCIS and Department of State forms.

benefits.title: End-to-End Support
benefits.description: We stand by you from the initial consultation until your case reaches a resolution.

title: Interview Preparation with Ex-Visa Officers
tagline: Gain the Confidence You Need for Your Embassy Interview
overview: Facing a consular interview can be daunting. Our interview preparation service pairs you with Ex-Visa Officers to provide real mock interviews, personalized feedback, and the training you need to succeed.

benefits.title: Real Mock Interview Practice
benefits.description: Experience realistic interview scenarios that mimic the actual consular environment.

benefits.title: Personalized Feedback Sessions
benefits.description: Receive actionable feedback on your answers, body language, and documentation presentation.

benefits.title: Confidence & Communication Training
benefits.description: Learn how to communicate your qualifications and intentions clearly and confidently to the visa officer.
